Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
Mass of substance		List-II
Number of atoms
A. $1.8$ mg waterI. $2\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
B. $9.8$ mg sulphuric acidII. $1.5\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
C. $1.8$ mg carbonIII. $3\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
D. $5.85$ mg salt (NaCl)IV. $7\times 10^{-4}\times N_A$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For A: Molar mass of $H_2O = 18$ g/mol. Moles of $H_2O = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^{-3}}{18} = 10^{-4}$. Since each $H_2O$ molecule has $3$ atoms, the number of atoms = $3 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

For B: Molar mass of $H_2SO_4 = 98$ g/mol. Moles of $H_2SO_4 = \dfrac{9.8 \times 10^{-3}}{98} = 10^{-4}$. Since each $H_2SO_4$ molecule has $7$ atoms, the number of atoms = $7 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

For C: Molar mass of $C = 12$ g/mol. Moles of $C = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^{-3}}{12} = 1.5 \times 10^{-4}$. The number of atoms = $1.5 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

For D: Molar mass of $NaCl = 58.5$ g/mol. Moles of $NaCl = \dfrac{5.85 \times 10^{-3}}{58.5} = 10^{-4}$. Since each $NaCl$ formula unit has $2$ atoms, the number of atoms = $2 \times 10^{-4} \times N_A$.

Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following contain the same number of atoms ? (Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of H, He, O and S are $1, 4, 16$ and $32$ respectively)
A. $2$ g of O$_2$ gas
B. $4$ g of SO$_2$ gas
C. $1400$ mL of O$_2$ at STP
D. $0.05$ L of He at STP
E. $0.0625$ mol of H$_2$ gas
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Number of atoms is calculated as the product of the number of moles, atomicity, and Avogadro's number ($N_A$).

For A: Moles of O$_2$ = $\dfrac{2}{32} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of O$_2$ is $2$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 2 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{8} N_A$

For B: Moles of SO$_2$ = $\dfrac{4}{64} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of SO$_2$ is $3$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 3 \times N_A = \dfrac{3}{16} N_A$

For C: Moles of O$_2$ at STP = $\dfrac{1400}{22400} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of O$_2$ is $2$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 2 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{8} N_A$

For D: Moles of He at STP = $\dfrac{0.05}{22.4} = \dfrac{1}{448}$ mol. Atomicity of He is $1$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{448} \times 1 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{448} N_A$

For E: Moles of H$_2$ = $0.0625 = \dfrac{1}{16}$ mol. Atomicity of H$_2$ is $2$.
Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{16} \times 2 \times N_A = \dfrac{1}{8} N_A$

Comparing the number of atoms, A, C, and E contain the same number of atoms.

Answer: A, C and E only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An oxide of iron contains $69.9\%$ iron, its empirical formula, is: (Given: Molar mass of Fe and O are $56$ and $16$ g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.)
questions.solution:
Mass percentage of $\text{Fe} = 69.9\%$

Mass percentage of $\text{O} = 100\% - 69.9\% = 30.1\%$

Number of moles of $\text{Fe} = \dfrac{69.9}{56} = 1.248$

Number of moles of $\text{O} = \dfrac{30.1}{16} = 1.881$

Molar ratio of $\text{Fe} : \text{O} = 1.248 : 1.881$

Dividing by the smallest value, the ratio is $\dfrac{1.248}{1.248} : \dfrac{1.881}{1.248} = 1 : 1.5$

Multiplying by $2$ to get the simplest whole number ratio, we get $2 : 3$.

The empirical formula is $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$.

Answer: $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What volume of hydrogen gas at STP would be liberated by action of $50\text{ mL}$ of $H_2SO_4$ of $50\%$ purity (density $= 1.3\text{ g mL}^{-1}$) on $20\text{ g}$ of zinc ?
Given : Molar mass of H, O, S, Zn are $1, 16, 32, 65\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Mass of $H_2SO_4$ solution $= 50 \times 1.3 = 65\text{ g}$

Mass of pure $H_2SO_4 = 65 \times \dfrac{50}{100} = 32.5\text{ g}$

Moles of $H_2SO_4 = \dfrac{32.5}{98} \approx 0.3316\text{ mol}$

Moles of $Zn = \dfrac{20}{65} \approx 0.3077\text{ mol}$

The balanced chemical equation is:
$Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2$

Since the moles of $Zn$ are less than the moles of $H_2SO_4$, $Zn$ is the limiting reagent.

Moles of $H_2$ produced $=$ Moles of $Zn = \dfrac{20}{65}\text{ mol}$

Volume of $H_2$ gas at STP $= \dfrac{20}{65} \times 22.4\text{ L} = 6.892\text{ L}$

Answer: $6.892\text{ L}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
How many grams of residue is obtained by heating $2.76$ g of silver carbonate?
(Given: Molar mass of C, O and Ag are $12$, $16$ and $108$ g mol$^{-1}$ respectively)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $Ag_2CO_3$ = $2 \times 108 + 12 + 3 \times 16 = 276$ g mol$^{-1}$

Number of moles of $Ag_2CO_3$ = $\dfrac{2.76}{276} = 0.01$ mol

The decomposition reaction of silver carbonate on heating is:

$Ag_2CO_3(s) \rightarrow 2Ag(s) + CO_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g)$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1$ mole of $Ag_2CO_3$ gives $2$ moles of Ag as residue.

Number of moles of Ag formed = $2 \times 0.01 = 0.02$ mol

Mass of Ag residue = $0.02 \times 108 = 2.16$ g

Answer: $2.16$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct order of total number of atoms present in
(A) $2$ moles of cyclohexane
(B) $684$ g of sucrose
(C) $90.8$ L of dihydrogen at STP
is:
questions.solution:
For (A):

Formula of cyclohexane is $C_6H_{12}$.

Number of atoms per molecule = $6 + 12 = 18$.

Total number of atoms in $2$ moles = $2 \times 18 \times N_A = 36 N_A$.

For (B):

Formula of sucrose is $C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}$.

Molar mass of sucrose = $342$ g/mol.

Number of moles = $\dfrac{684}{342} = 2$ moles.

Number of atoms per molecule = $12 + 22 + 11 = 45$.

Total number of atoms = $2 \times 45 \times N_A = 90 N_A$.

For (C):

Formula of dihydrogen is $H_2$.

Number of moles at STP = $\dfrac{90.8}{22.7} = 4$ moles.

Number of atoms per molecule = $2$.

Total number of atoms = $4 \times 2 \times N_A = 8 N_A$.

Comparing the total number of atoms:

$90 N_A > 36 N_A > 8 N_A$

Therefore, the correct order is $B > A > C$.

Answer: $B>A>C$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Number of moles and number of molecules in $1.4187$ L of $SO_2$ at STP respectively are:
questions.solution:
Volume of $SO_2$ at STP $= 1.4187$ L

Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is approximately $22.414$ L.

Number of moles $n = \dfrac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar Volume}} = \dfrac{1.4187}{22.414} = 0.0633$

Number of molecules $= n \times N_A$

Number of molecules $= 0.0633 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.812 \times 10^{22}$

Answer: $0.0633; 3.812 \times 10^{22}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ratio of mass percentage (w/w) of C : H in a hydrocarbon is $12 : 1$. It has two carbon atoms. The weight (in g) of $CO_2(g)$ formed when $3.38$ g of this hydrocarbon is completely burnt in oxygen is : (Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16)
questions.solution:
Ratio of mass percentage of C : H = $12 : 1$

Ratio of moles of C : H = $\dfrac{12}{12} : \dfrac{1}{1} = 1 : 1$

The empirical formula is $CH$. Since the hydrocarbon has two carbon atoms, its molecular formula is $C_2H_2$.

Molar mass of $C_2H_2 = 2 \times 12 + 2 \times 1 = 26$ g mol$^{-1}$

Moles of $C_2H_2$ in $3.38$ g = $\dfrac{3.38}{26} = 0.13$ mol

The combustion reaction is:

$C_2H_2 + \dfrac{5}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + H_2O$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of $C_2H_2$ produces $2$ moles of $CO_2$.

Moles of $CO_2$ produced = $2 \times 0.13 = 0.26$ mol

Molar mass of $CO_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44$ g mol$^{-1}$

Weight of $CO_2$ formed = $0.26 \times 44 = 11.44$ g

Answer: $11.44$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the given reaction:
$\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}+2 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaCl}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_{2}$
If $90 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}$ is added to 300 mL of HCl which contains $38.55 \% \mathrm{HCl}$ by mass and has density $1.13 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}$, then which of the following option is correct ?
Given molar mass of $\mathrm{H}, \mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{Ca}$ and O are 1, 35.5, 40 and $16 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Molar masses: HCl = 36.5, CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol
HCl solution: mass = 300 × 1.13 = 339 g
HCl present: 339 × 0.3855 = 130.74 g = 130.74/36.5 = 3.58 mol
CaCO₃: 90/100 = 0.9 mol
Reaction: $CaCO_3 + 2HCl → CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2$
HCl required: 0.9 × 2 = 1.8 mol
HCl available: 3.58 mol > 1.8 mol
CaCO₃ is limiting. HCl remaining: (3.58 - 1.8) × 36.5 = 1.78 × 36.5 = 64.97 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{A}+2 \mathrm{~B} \longrightarrow \mathrm{AB}_{2}$
36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass: $60 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) and 56.0 g of ' $\mathrm{B}^{\prime}$ (Molar mass: $80 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. 'A' is the limiting reagent.
B. $77.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ is formed.
C. Molar mass of $A B_{2}$ is $140 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.
D. $15.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Reaction: A + 2B → AB₂.
Moles of A = 36.0/60 = 0.6 mol;
Moles of B = 56.0/80 = 0.7 mol.
A requires 1.2 mol of B but only 0.7 available, so B is limiting reagent.
So, (A) False - B is limiting.
(B) AB₂ formed = 0.7/2 = 0.35 mol;
Molar mass AB₂ = 60 + 2(80) = 220 g/mol;
Mass = 0.35 × 220 = 77 g True.
(C) False - Molar mass is 220 g/mol.
(D) A remaining = 0.6 - 0.35 = 0.25 mol = 15 g True.
Correct statements: B and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the reaction,
$2 \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s})+6 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq})+6 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+3 \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$
options: $11.2 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ at STP is produced for every mole of HCl consumed.
$33.6 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ is produced regardless of temperature and pressure for every mole of Al that reacts.
$67.2 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ at STP is produced for every mole of Al that reacts.
questions.solution:
Reaction: $2\text{Al}(s) + 6\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(aq) + 6\text{Cl}^-(aq) + 3\text{H}_2(g)$
Checking each option:
(1) Per 1 mole HCl: From stoichiometry, 6 mol HCl produces 3 mol H₂, so 1 mol HCl produces 0.5 mol H₂ = 11.2 L at STP. TRUE
(2) Per 1 mole Al: 2 mol Al produces 3 mol H₂, so 1 mol Al produces 1.5 mol H₂ = 33.6 L at STP only, not regardless of T and P. FALSE
(3) Volume ratio at same T,P: 6 mol HCl : 3 mol H₂ = 2:1, so 12 L HCl : 6 L H₂. TRUE
(4) Per 1 mole Al: 1.5 mol H₂ = 33.6 L, not 67.2 L. FALSE
Option (1) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Aqueous HCl reacts with $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}(\mathrm{~s})$ to form $\mathrm{MnCl}_{2}(\mathrm{aq}), \mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(l)$. What is the weight (in g) of $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ liberated when 8.7 g of $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}(\mathrm{~s})$ is reacted with excess aqueous HCl solution?
(Given Molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{Mn}=55, \mathrm{Cl}=35.5, \mathrm{O}=16, \mathrm{H}=1$)
questions.solution:
The balanced redox equation is: $\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MnCl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Molar mass of MnO₂ = 55 + 32 = 87 g/mol.
Moles of MnO₂ = $\frac{8.7}{87} = 0.1$ mol.
From stoichiometry, 1 mol MnO₂ produces 1 mol Cl₂, so 0.1 mol produces 0.1 mol Cl₂.
Mass of Cl₂ = $0.1 \times 71 = 7.1$ g.

Statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 80 mL of a hydrocarbon on mixing with 264 mL of oxygen in a closed U-tube undergoes complete combustion. The residual gases after cooling to 273 K occupy 224 mL. When the system is treated with KOH solution, the volume decreases to 64 mL. The formula of the hydrocarbon is :
questions.solution:
KOH absorbs $CO_2$. Volume of $CO_2$ produced = $224 - 64 = 160$ mL
Unreacted $O_2 = 64$ mL, so $O_2$ consumed = $264 - 64 = 200$ mL
For hydrocarbon $C_xH_y$: $\frac{CO_2}{\text{Hydrocarbon}} = \frac{160}{80} = 2 \Rightarrow x = 2$
$O_2$ consumed per mole = $x + \frac{y}{4} = \frac{200}{80} = 2.5$
$2 + \frac{y}{4} = 2.5 \Rightarrow y = 2$
Hydrocarbon is $C_2H_2$

questions.q:
Butane reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water following the equation given below
$\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}(\mathrm{~g})+\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{~g})+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$
If 174.0 kg of butane is mixed with 320.0 kg of $\mathrm{O}_2$, the volume of water formed in litres is ________.(Nearest integer)
[Given : (a) Molar mass of $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{H}, \mathrm{O}$ are 12, 1, $16 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively, (b) Density of water $\left.=1 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}+\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_2+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\
& 3 \times 10^3 \quad 10 \times 10^3
\end{aligned}$
Moles of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ formed $=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}=5 \times \frac{2}{13} \times 10 \times 10^3$
Then $\mathrm{w}_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}=\frac{10^5}{13} \times 18$
$=1.3846 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~g}$
Volume of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ will be $=138.46$ litre.
Ans. 138

Moles of ' C ' \(=$\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CO}_2}=\frac{1.46}{44}=$0.033\)
Moles of ' C ' \(=$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{C}}=$0.033 $\times$12\)
Moles of 'H' \(=2 $\times \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}=$2 $\times \frac{0.567}{18}=$0.063\)
Mass of ' H ' \(=0.0063\)
Mass of Oxygen \((\mathrm{O})=$1-\left(\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{c}}+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{H}}\right)\) \(=1-(0.033 \times$12+0.063 $\times$1)=0.541 $\mathrm{gm}\)
Moles of ' O ' \(=\frac{0.541}{16}=$0.033\)
Empirical formula \(=$\mathrm{CH}}_{2} \mathrm{O}$\)
Empirical formula mass \(=30\).

mole of $\mathrm{Fe}=\frac{3}{4} \times 10^4$

& 10=\frac{10}{M} \times 100 \\

questions.q: $10mL$ of gaseous hydrocarbon on combustion gives $40mL$ of ${CO}_{2}\left(g\right)$ and $50mL$ of water vapour. Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is _______.
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction can be represented as 

${C}_{x}{H}_{y} + \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right){O}_{2} \to {xCO}_{2} + {yH}_{2}O$

At STP, $1$ mole of any gas occupies $22 . 4L$

$10mL$ of hydrocarbon, $50mL$ of water and $40mL$ of carbon dioxide corresponds to $0 . 45, 2 . 23$,  and $1 . 79$moles respectively.

Hence, the combustion of $1$ mole of hydrocarbon will produce $5$ moles of water and $4$ moles of carbon dioxide.

Thus, the molecular formula contains $4$ carbon atoms and $10$ hydrogen atoms.

The hydrocarbon is ${C}_{4}{H}_{10}$ and the combustion reaction is 

${C}_{4}{H}_{10} + 6 . 5{O}_{2} \to 4{CO}_{2} + 5{H}_{2}O$

$x + y = 4 + 10 = 14$

Hence the Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is $14$.

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction:

$3{PbCl}_{2} + 2{\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{3}{PO}_{4} \to {Pb}_{3}{\left({PO}_{4}\right)}_{2} + 6{NH}_{4}Cl$

If $72mmol{PbCl}_{2}$ is mixed with $50mmol$ of ${\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{3}{PO}_{4},$ then amount of ${Pb}_{3}{\left({PO}_{4}\right)}_{2}$ formed in $mmol$. (nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The reaction is given as,

$3{PbCl}_{2} + 2{\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{3}{PO}_{4} \to {Pb}_{3}{\left({PO}_{4}\right)}_{2} + 6{NH}_{4}Cl$

The products formed in the above reaction is ${Pb}_{3}{\left({PO}_{4}\right)}_{2}\text{and}{NH}_{4}Cl$  .

According to the above stoichiometric equation, three mole of each lead chloride and two moles of ${\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{3}{PO}_{4}$ is required to make one mole of ${Pb}_{3}{\left({PO}_{4}\right)}_{2}\text{and}6\text{moles of}{NH}_{4}Cl$   

Here the Limiting Reagent is ${PbCl}_{2}$

$mmol$ of ${Pb}_{3} ( {PO}_{4}{)}_{2}$ formed

$= \dfrac{mmol\text{of}{PbCl}_{2}\text{reacted}}{3} = \dfrac{72}{3}$

$= 24m mol$

questions.q:
A sample of ${CaCO}_{3}$ and ${MgCO}_{3}$ weighed $2 .21 g$ is ignited to constant weight of $1 .152 g$. The composition of the mixture is:

(Given molar mass in $g{mol}^{- 1}$, ${CaCO}_{3}: 100, {MgCO}_{3}: 84$)
questions.solution:
$CaC{O}_{3}\left(s\right)\overset{\Delta}{\to}CaO\left(s\right) + C{O}_{2}\left(g\right)$

$MgC{O}_{3}\left(s\right)\overset{\Delta}{\to}MgO\left(s\right) + C{O}_{2}\left(g\right)$

Let the weight of $CaC{O}_{3}$ be $xgm$

$∴$ weight of $MgC{O}_{3} = \left(2 .21 - x\right)gm$

Moles of $CaC{O}_{3}$ decomposed = moles of $CaO$ formed

$\dfrac{x}{100} =$ moles of $CaO$ formed

$∴$ weight of $CaO$ formed $= \dfrac{x}{100} \times 56$
Moles of $MgC{O}_{3}$ decomposed = moles of $MgO$ formed

$\dfrac{\left(2 .21 - x\right)}{84} =$ moles of $MgO$ formed

$∴$  weight of $MgO$ formed $= \dfrac{2 .21 - x}{84} \times 40$⇒ \dfrac{2 .21 - x}{84} \times 40 + \dfrac{x}{100} \times 56 = 1 .152$

$∴ x = 1 .187 g =$ weight of $CaC{O}_{3}$ and weight of $MgC{O}_{3} = 1 .023 g$

questions.q: Number of moles of methane required to produce $22g{CO}_{2 ( g )}$ after combustion is $x \times {10}^{– 2}$ moles. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
${CH}_{4} + 2{O}_{2} \to {CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Gram molecular mass of ${CO}_{2} = 12 + 2 ( 16 ) = 44g / mol$

From the reaction, it is clear that $1$ mole of methane on complete combustion produces $44g$ ($1$ mole) of carbon dioxide.

Therefore moles of ${CH}_{4}$ required to produce $22g$ of ${CO}_{2}$ are:

$= \dfrac{1}{44} \times 22 = 0 . 5mol = 50 \times {10}^{- 2}mol$

Hence, $m = 50$

$⇒ x = 2$

$∴$ Formula of metal chloride is ${MCl}_{2}$

questions.q: If $5$ moles of ${BaCl}_{2}$ is mixed with $2$ moles of ${Na}_{3}{PO}_{4},$ the maximum number of moles of ${Ba}_{3}{\left({PO}_{4}\right)}_{2}$formed is $_________$ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction between ${BaCl}_{2}$ and ${Na}_{3}{PO}_{4}$ is:

$3{BaCl}_{2} + 2{Na}_{3}{PO}_{4} \to {Ba}_{3} ( {PO}_{4}{)}_{2} + 6NaCl$

$5$ moles of barium chloride will require $\dfrac{5 \times 2}{3} = 3 . 3$ moles of sodium phosphate.

Here, sodium phosphate is the limiting reagent.
$2$ moles of sodium phosphate produce $1$ mole of barium phosphate.

Thus,$2$ moles of sodium phosphate will produce$1$ mole of barium phosphate.

Hence, the maximum no. of moles of ${Ba}_{3} ( {PO}_{4}{)}_{2}$that can be formed is one mole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a hydrocarbon $A$ undergoes complete combustion it requires $11$ equivalents of oxygen and produces $4$ equivalents of water. What is the molecular formula of $A$?
questions.solution:
By using the formula of combustion analysis:

${C}_{x}{H}_{y} + \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right){O}_{2} \to {CO}_{2} + \dfrac{y}{2}{H}_{2}O$

Given, $\left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right)a = 11a$

$x + \dfrac{y}{4} = 11$

$\left(\dfrac{y}{2}\right)a = 4a$

$y = 8$,

then $x + \dfrac{8}{4} = 11$

$x = 11 - \dfrac{8}{4}$

$x = 9$

Formula $= {C}_{9}{H}_{8}$

When coal of purity $60 %$ is allowed to burn in presence of insufficient oxygen, $60 %$ of carbon is converted into ' $CO$' and the remaining is converted into '${CO}_{2}$'.

$1$ mole

$= 1800kJ$

$= 12 \times 400$

$= 4800$

To find the limiting reagent we can divide given number of moles with Stoichiometric coefficients, whichever will be the lower will be limiting reagent.

questions.q: Chlorophyll extracted from the crushed green leaves was dissolved in water to make $2L$ solution of $Mg$ of concentration $48 \mathrm{ppm}$. The number of atoms of $Mg$ in this solution is $x \times {10}^{20}$ atoms. The value of $x$ is (Nearest Integer) (Given : Atomic mass of $Mg$ is $24g{mol}^{- 1}$, ${N}_{A} = 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23}{mol}^{- 1}$)

Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria that is essential for photosynthesis. Its central structure is an aromatic porphyrin ring system with a sequestered magnesium atom.

$= 48 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3}g$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 3}$

Number of $Mg$ atoms $= 4 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23} = 4 \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{20}$

$= 4 \times 6 . 02 \times {10}^{20}$

$= 24 . 08 \times {10}^{20}$

$∴ x = 24 . 08$

questions.q: $56 . 0L$ of nitrogen gas is mixed with excess of hydrogen gas and it is found that $20L$ of ammonia gas is produced, The volume of unused nitrogen gas is found to be_____ $L$.
questions.solution: Gay-Lussac's Law proposes a relationship between the combining volumes of gases with respect to the reactants and gaseous products. According to this law, when gases react together to produce gaseous products, the volumes of reactants and products bear a simple whole number ratio with each other, provided volumes are measured at same temperature and pressure.

Production of iron in blast furnace follows the following equation

${Fe}_{3}{O}_{4}\left(s\right) + 4CO\left(g\right) \to 3Fe\left(l\right) + 4{CO}_{2}\left(g\right)

when $4 . 640kg of {Fe}_{3}{O}_{4} and 2 . 520kg of CO$ are allowed to react then the amount of iror (in $g$) produced is :$

Molar Atomic mass $\left({gmolm}^{- 1}\right): O = 16$

Molar Atomic mass $\left({gmolm}^{- 1}\right): C = 12$]
questions.solution:
Moles of ${Fe}_{3}{O}_{4} = \dfrac{4 . 640 \times {10}^{3}}{232} = 20$

Moles of $CO = \dfrac{2 . 52 \times {10}^{3}}{28} = 90$

So limiting Reagent $= {Fe}_{3}{O}_{4}$

So moles of Fe formed $= 60$

Weight of $Fe = 60 \times 56 = 3360gms$

(c) % of $H = \dfrac{6}{62} \times 100 = 7 . 677$%

The percentage of Hydrogen in the given organic compound is equal to $6 . 465 %$ which is approximately equal to the percentage of hydrogen in ${CH}_{3}COOHandHCHO$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $CNG$ is an important transportation fuel. When $100gCNG$ is mixed with $208g$ oxygen in vehicles, it leads to the formation of ${CO}_{2}$ and ${H}_{2}O$ and produces large quantity of heat during this combustion, then the amount of carbon dioxide, produced in grams is [nearest integer] [Assume CNG to be methane]
questions.solution:
${CH}_{4} + 2{O}_{2} ⟶ {CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

$\dfrac{100}{16}\dfrac{208}{32}$

$\dfrac{Numberofmoles}{stoichiometriccoefficient}for{CH}_{4} = \dfrac{6 . 25}{1}\dfrac{Numberofmoles}{stoichiometriccoefficient}for{O}_{2} = \dfrac{6 . 5}{2} = 3 . 25$

The reagent with lower ratio of number of moles to stoichiometric coefficient is called limiting reagent.

Hence, ${O}_{2}$ is limiting reagent

Limiting reagent decides the amount of product,

As per the equation 2 moles of ${O}_{2}$ gives rise to 1 mole of ${CO}_{2}$, So 6.5 moles of ${O}_{2}$ gives $\dfrac{6 . 5}{2}$ moles of ${CO}_{2}$

$⇒ {nCO}_{2} = \dfrac{6 . 5}{2}$

So mass of ${CO}_{2} = \dfrac{6 . 5}{2} \times 44 = 143gm$

${nCH}_{4} = \dfrac{81}{18} \times 2 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{81}{36}$

$= 225 \times {10}^{- 2}$

Hence, the number of moles of methane is $225 \times {10}^{- 2}$

If the rate of appearance of ${Cr}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3}$ is $2 . 67mol{min}^{- 1}$ at a particular time, the rate of disappearance of ${C}_{2}{H}_{6}O$ at the same time is mol ${min}^{- 1} .$ (Nearest integer)

$\dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{- d\left[{C}_{2}{H}_{6}O\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d\left[{Cr}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3}\right]}{dt}$

$\dfrac{1}{3}$ (Rate of disappearance of $\left{C}_{2}{H}_{6}O\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ (Rate of disappearance of $\left{Cr}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3}\right)$

Rate of disappearance of ${C}_{2}{H}_{6}O = \left(\dfrac{2 . 67mol / min \times 3}{2}\right) = 4 . 005mol / min$

questions.q: The formula of a gaseous hydrocarbon which requires 6 times of its own volume of ${O}_{2}$ for complete oxidation and produces $4$ times its own volume of ${CO}_{2}$ is ${C}_{x}{H}_{y} .$ The value of $y$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Combustion reaction.

${C}_{x}{H}_{y ( g )} + \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right){O}_{2}\left(g\right) \to {xCO}_{2}\left(g\right) + \dfrac{y}{2}{H}_{2}O\left(ℓ\right)$

$\begin{cases}V & 6V & - \\ - & - & Vx = 4V\end{cases}$

$⇒ x = 4$

Since: $\left(I\right){Vo}_{2} = 6 \times {V}_{{C}_{x}{H}_{y}}$

$⇒ V\left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right) = 6V$

questions.q: The ammonia $\left({NH}_{3}\right)$ released on quantitative reaction of $0.6g$ urea $\left({NH}_{2}CON{H}_{2}\right)$ with sodium hydroxide $\left(NaOH\right)$ can be neutralized by
questions.solution:
${NH}_{2}{CONH}_{2} + 2NaOH \to 2{NH}_{3} + {Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}$

By, stoichiometry, $1mol$ of urea gives $2mol${NH}_{3}$

Moles of urea =$= \dfrac{0 . 6gm}{60gm / mol} = 0 . 01mol$

So, $0 . 01$ mole urea produce $0 . 02$ mole ${NH}_{3}$

To neutralize ammonia $HCl$ is required

${NH}_{3} + HCl \to {NH}_{4}Cl$

By equation, it is clear that $1mol$ of ammonia is neutralized by 1mol of $HCl$.

So, $0 . 02mol$ of ammonia neutralized by $0 . 02mol$ of $HCl$

$∴ MoleofHCl = 0.02mole$

$EquivalentofHCl = normality \times volume = 0 . 2N \times 100mL = 0 . 02equivalent$

As $n$-factor of $HCl$ is $1$, so $numberofequivalents = numberofmoles = 0 . 02moles$

Hence, option $3$ is correct.

questions.q: At $300K$ and $1$ atmospheric pressure, $10mL$ of a hydrocarbon required $55mL$ of ${O}_{2}$ for complete combustion, and $40mL$ of $C{O}_{2}$ is formed. The formula of the hydrocarbon is:
questions.solution:
Let hydrocarbon is ${C}_{x}{H}_{y}$

$10x = 40$ ; x = 4 and $10\left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right) = 55$
$\left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right) = \dfrac{55}{10}$
$x + \dfrac{y}{4} = 5.5$
Put the value of $x$
$4 + \dfrac{y}{4} = 5.5$
$\dfrac{y}{4} = 5 . 5 - 4$
$\dfrac{y}{4} = 1 . 5$ then $y = 6$
Hence hydrocarbon is ${C}_{4}{H}_{6}$

Mass of fatty acid $= 0.027g$ in $10ml$ solution

Density of fatty acid $0.9$ g/cc

Volume of fatty acid $= \dfrac{0.027}{0.9} = 0.03cc$

Area of plate $= \pi{r}^{2} = 3 \times {10}^{2} = 300c{m}^{2}$

Height of fatty acid layer $= \dfrac{volume}{area} = \dfrac{0.03}{300} = {10}^{- 4}cm$ = ${10}^{- 6}m$

questions.q: For per gram of reactant, the maximum quantity of $\mathrm{N}_2$ gas is produced in which of the following thermal decomposition reactions? (Given: Atomic wt. : $\mathrm{Cr}=52 \mathrm{u}, \mathrm{Ba}=137 \mathrm{u}$ ).
questions.solution:
(a) Molar mass of Ba $\left(\mathrm{N}_3\right)_2(\mathrm{~s})=221 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ 1 mole of $\mathrm{Ba}\left(\mathrm{N}_3\right)_2(\mathrm{~s})$ will give 3 moles of $\mathrm{N}_2$ hence $\frac{1 \mathrm{~g}}{221 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}}$ moles of $\mathrm{Ba}\left(\mathrm{N}_3\right)_2(\mathrm{~s})$ will give $3 \times \frac{1}{221}=0.014$ moles of $\mathrm{N}_2$
(b) Molar mass of $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7=252 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$. 1 mole of $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$ will give 1 mole of $\mathrm{N}_2$ hence $\frac{1 \mathrm{~g}}{252 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}}$ moles of $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$ will give $1 \times \frac{1}{252}=0.0039$ moles of $\mathrm{N}_2$
(c) Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}_3=17 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$. 2 mole of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ will give 1 mole of $\mathrm{N}_2$
hence $\frac{1 \mathrm{~g}}{17 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}}$ moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ will give

$\frac{1}{2 \times 17}=$0.0297 $\text{ moles$ of $} \mathrm{N}_{2} \text{. }

(d) Molar mass of  \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{NO}_3=$80 $\mathrm{~g}$/ $\mathrm{mol}. 1 mole$ of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{NO}_3 will give 1 mole of  \mathrm{N}_2 hence \frac{1 \mathrm{~g}}{80 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}} moles  \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{NO}_3 will give

1 \times \frac{1}{80}=0.0125 \text{ moles of } \mathrm{N}_{2}$

Hence Thermal decomposition of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ will produce maximum amount of $\mathrm{N}_2$.

questions.q:
A sample of $\mathrm{NaClO}_3$ is converted by heat to $\mathrm{NaCl}$ with a loss of $0.16 \mathrm{~g}$ of oxygen. The residue is dissolved in water and precipitated as $\mathrm{AgCl}$. The mass of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ (in $\mathrm{g}$) obtained will be:
(Given: Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgCl}=143.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
No. of moles of oxygen in $0.16 \mathrm{~g}$ of oxygen molecule
$=\frac{0.16 \mathrm{~g}}{32 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}}=0.005 \mathrm{~mole} 2 \mathrm{NaClO}_3 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{NaCl}+3 \mathrm{O}_2$
According to the reaction, 
$3$ moles of $\mathrm{O}_2=2$ moles of $\mathrm{NaCl} =2$ moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgCl}=143.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol} 0.005$ moles of $\mathrm{O}_2$ will ppt. $=0.005 \times \frac{2}{3}$ moles $\mathrm{AgCl}=0.0033 \text{ moles of } \mathrm{AgCl}\therefore$ Mass of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ (in $\mathrm{g}$) obtained will be 
$=143.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol} \times 0.0033$ moles $=0.48 \mathrm{~g}$.

The most abundant elements by mass in the body of a healthy human adult are:

Oxygen (61.4%); Carbon (22.9%), Hydrogen (10.0%); and Nitrogen (2.6%). The weight which a 75kg person would gain if all ${}^{1}H$ atoms are replaced by ${}^{2}H$ atoms is:
questions.solution:
Weight of Hydrogen in body of 75 kg person $= 75 \times \dfrac{10}{100} = 7 .5 kg$

On replacing ${}^{1}H$ by ${}^{2}H$ , the new weight of $H = 7 .5 \times 2 = 15kg$

Weight increase = $7 . 5kg$

questions.q: The amount of arsenic pentasulphide that can be obtained when $35 . 5g$ arsenic acid is treated with excess ${H}_{2}S$ in the presence of conc. $HCl$ (assuming $100 %$ conversion) is
questions.solution:
$2{H}_{3}As{O}_{4} + 5{H}_{2}S\overset{Conc . HCl}{\to}A{s}_{2}{S}_{5} + 8{H}_{2}O$

$2$ moles of Arsenic Acid $\to$1$ mole of Arsenic Pentasulphide

$1$ moles of Arsenic Acid $\to$1 / 2$ mole of Arsenic Pentasulphide

$Molarmassof{H}_{3}As{O}_{4} = 141; MolarmassofA{s}_{2}{S}_{5} = 308$

$∴$ Number of moles of ${H}_{3}As{O}_{4} = \dfrac{35.5}{141} = 0.25$

$∴$ Number of moles of $A{s}_{2}{S}_{5} = \dfrac{0.25}{2} = 0.125mol$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
At $300K$ and $1atm$, $15mL$ of a gaseous hydrocarbon requires $375mL$ air containing $20 % {O}_{2}$ by volume, for complete combustion. After combustion, the gases occupy $345mL$. Assuming that the water formed is in liquid form and the volumes were measured at the same temperature and pressure, the formula of the hydrocarbon is:
(Assume complete combustion of reactant)
questions.solution:
Volume of ${N}_{2}$ in air$= 375 \times 0.8 = 300ml$
Volume of ${O}_{2}$ in air$= 375 \times 0.2 = 75ml$
$\begin{cases}{\text{C}}_{\text{x}} {\text{H}}_{\text{y}} & + & \left(\text{x} + \dfrac{\text{y}}{4}\right) {\text{O}}_{2} & ⟶ & {\text{xCO}}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right) & + & \dfrac{\text{y}}{2} {\text{H}}_{2} \text{O} \left(ℓ\right) \\ 1 5 \text{ml} & & 1 5 \left(\text{x} + \dfrac{\text{y}}{4}\right) & & & & \\ 0 & & 0 & & 1 5 \text{x} & & -\end{cases}$
After combustion, total volume
$345 = {V}_{{N}_{2}} + {V}_{{CO}_{2}}$
$345 = 300 + 15x$
$x = 3$
Volume of ${O}_{2}$ used
$15\left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right) = 75$
$x + \dfrac{y}{4} = 5$
$y = 8$
So, hydrocarbon is${C}_{3}{H}_{8}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the following reaction:

$A + 2B + 3C ⇌ A{B}_{2}{C}_{3}$
$6 . 0g$ of $A$, $6.0 \times {10}^{23}$ atoms of $B$ and $0 . 036mol$ of $C$ reacted and formed $4 . 8g$ of compound $A{B}_{2}{C}_{3}$. If the atomic mass of $A$ and $C$ are $60$ and $80amu$, respectively. What is the atomic mass of $B$ in $amu$? (Avogadro number$= 6 \times {10}^{23}$)
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases} & \text{A} & + & 2 \text{B} & + & 3 \text{C} & \to & {\text{AB}_{2} {\text{C}_{3} \\ & 6 \text{g} & & 6 \times 1 {0}^{2 3} \text{atoms} & & \text{0.036} moles & & \\ \text{Moles} & \dfrac{6}{6 0} & & \dfrac{6 \times 1 {0}^{2 3}}{6 \times 1 {0}^{2 3}} & & & & \\ & \text{0.1 mole} & & \text{1.0 mole} & & \text{0.036 moles} & & \end{cases}$

$\left(\dfrac{0.1}{1}, \dfrac{1.0}{2}, \dfrac{0.036}{3}; theleastvalueis0.012, i . e . , Cisthelimitingreagent\right)$
$0 . 036moles of C$ provides $0 . 012moles of A{B}_{2}{C}_{3}$.

$0 . 012moles of A{B}_{2}{C}_{3}$ weighs $4 .8 g$
$1mole of {AB}_{2}{C}_{3}$ weighs $\dfrac{4 .8}{0 .012} = 400g{mol}^{- 1}$
$400 = 60 + 2B + 3 \times 80$
$B = 50amu$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ratio of masses of oxygen and nitrogen in a particular gaseous mixture is 1 : 4. The ratio of number of their molecules is:
questions.solution:
Let the mass of oxygen be $x$ gm
$∴$ Mass of nitrogen = $4x$ gm
Number of molecules = 6.023 x 1023 x number of moles
$∴ \text{Ratio} = \dfrac{\text{6.023} \times 1 {0}^{2 3} \times \text{no. of moles of oxygen}}{\text{6.023} \times 1 {0}^{2 3} \times \text{no. of moles of nitrogen}}$
$= \dfrac{\dfrac{{\text{m}}_{{\text{O}}_{2}}}{{\text{M}}_{{\text{O}}_{2}}}}{\dfrac{{\text{m}}_{{\text{N}}_{2}}}{{\text{M}}_{{\text{N}}_{2}}}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{3 2}}{\dfrac{4 x}{2 8}}$
$= \dfrac{7}{3 2} = \text{7 : 32}$
questions.question: The ratio of masses of oxygen and nitrogen in a particular gaseous mixture is 1 : 4. The ratio of number of their molecules is:
questions.explanation:
Let the mass of oxygen be $x$ gm
$∴$ Mass of nitrogen = $4x$ gm
Number of molecules = 6.023 x 1023 x number of moles
$∴ \text{Ratio} = \dfrac{\text{6.023} \times 1 {0}^{2 3} \times \text{no. of moles of oxygen}}{\text{6.023} \times 1 {0}^{2 3} \times \text{no. of moles of nitrogen}}$
$= \dfrac{\dfrac{{\text{m}}_{{\text{O}}_{2}}}{{\text{M}}_{{\text{O}}_{2}}}}{\dfrac{{\text{m}}_{{\text{N}}_{2}}}{{\text{M}}_{{\text{N}}_{2}}}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{3 2}}{\dfrac{4 x}{2 8}}$
$= \dfrac{7}{3 2} = \text{7 : 32}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $10 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $2(\mathrm{M}) \mathrm{~NaOH}$ solution is added to $200 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.5$\mathrm{(M)}$ of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution. What is the final concentration ?
questions.solution:
From molarity equation
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{M}_1 \mathrm{V}_1+\mathrm{M}_2 \mathrm{V}_2=\mathrm{MV}_{\text{(total) }} \\
& 2 \times \frac{10}{1000}+0.5 \times \frac{200}{1000}=\mathrm{M} \times \frac{210}{1000} \\
& 120=\mathrm{M} \times 210 \\
& \mathrm{M}=\frac{120}{210}=0.57 \mathrm{ M}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Experimentally it was found that a metal oxide has formula ${M}_{0.98}O$. Metal M, is present as ${M}^{2 +}$ and ${M}^{3 +}$ in its oxide. Fraction of the metal which exists as ${M}^{3 +}$ would be:
questions.solution:
Consider one mole of the oxide, then

Moles of M = 0.98; Moles of O2- = 1

Let 'x' moles of M are in +3 oxidation state, then Moles of M2+ = 0.98-x

On doing charge balancing we get

(0.98 - x)2 + 3x = 2

Or 1.96 - 2x + 3x - 2 = 0

Or x = 0.04

$∴ % of{M}^{3 +} = \dfrac{0 .04}{0 .98} \times 100 = 4 .08 %$

questions.q: A transition metal $M$ forms a volatile chloride which has a vapour density of $94.8$. If it contains $74.75 \%$ of chlorine the formula of the metal chloride will be
questions.solution:
$74.75 \%$ of chlorine means $74.75 \mathrm{~g}$ chlorine is present in $100 \mathrm{~g}$ of metal chloride.
Weight of metal $=100 \mathrm{~g}-74.75 \mathrm{~g}$=25.25 \mathrm{~g}$
Equivalent weight
$
\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{\text { weight of metal }}{\text { weight of chlorine }} \times 35.5 \\
& =\frac{25.25}{74.75} \times 35.5=12
\end{aligned}
$
Valency of metal
$
\begin{array}{r}
=\frac{2 \times \text { V.D. }}{\text { Equivalent wt. of metal }+35.5} \\
=\frac{2 \times 94.8}{12+35.5}=4
\end{array}
$
$\therefore$ Formula of compound $=\mathrm{MCl}_4$

questions.q: Number of atoms in $558.5$ gram Fe (at.wt. of $\mathrm{Fe}=55.85 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) is
options:
twice that in 60 g carbon

$6.023 \times 10^{22}$

half that in $8 \mathrm{g} \mathrm{~He}$

$558.5 \times 6.023 \times 10^{23}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Fe}($ no. of moles $)=\frac{558.5}{55.85}=10$ moles
$C$ (no. of moles $)=60 / 12=5$ moles.
